[[File:Ferula tingitana MHNT.BOT.2025.29.2.jpg|thumb|''Ferula tingitana'' ([[MHNT]])]]

'''''Ferula tingitana''''', the '''giant Tangier fennel''', is a species of the [[Apiaceae]] genus ''[[Ferula]]''. Despite the name, the plant is not a type of fennel proper, which belongs to another genus (''[[Foeniculum]]'').

''Ferula tingitana'' is a tall perennial [[herbaceous|herb]]. It has alternate leaf arrangement and yellow, unisexual flowers which, like other [[Apiaceae]], grow in [[umbels]].  
It grows in [[scrubland]] ([[Garrigue#Similar ecoregions|batha and phrygana]]) and rocky areas.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://flora.huji.ac.il/browse.asp?lang=en&action=specie&specie=FERTIN |work=Flora of Israel Online |title=Ferula tingitana L. |publisher=The Hebrew University of Jerusalem |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120930170723/http://flora.huji.ac.il/browse.asp?lang=en&action=specie&specie=FERTIN |archivedate=2012-09-30 }}</ref>  Its range is the Mediterranean coast, in [[Spain]], [[Morocco]], [[Lebanon]], [[Syria]], [[Israel]], [[Cyprus]], and [[Turkey]].<ref>{{ cite web | url = http://data.gbif.org/species/3636208/ | title = ''Ferula tingitana'' L. | publisher = Global Biodiversity Information Facility }}</ref>
<ref>{{ cite web | url = http://euromed.luomus.fi/euromed_map.php?taxon=344219&size=medium | title = ''Ferula tingitana'' L. | publisher = The Euro+Med PlantBase }}</ref>
In the 1980s there was chemical interest in [[ester]]s and [[ether]]s extracted from it.<ref>{{cite journal | title = A New Sesquiterpene Ester from ''Ferula tingitana'' |author1=Miski, M. |author2=Ulubelen, A. |authorlink2=Ayhan Ulubelen |author3=Mabry, T. J. | journal = Journal of Natural Products | year = 1986 | volume = 49 | issue = 4 | pages = 657–660 | doi = 10.1021/np50046a016 | pmid = 3783161 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title = Sesquiterpene-Coumarin Ethers of ''Ferula tingitana'' |author1=Miski, M. |author2=Ulubelen, A. |authorlink2=Ayhan Ulubelen | journal = Journal of Natural Products | year = 1985 | volume = 48 | issue = 2 | pages = 326–327 | doi = 10.1021/np50038a024 | pmid = 4009187 }}</ref>

This species has been considered to have abortive and [[menstruation]]-inducing properties.<ref>{{cite journal | title = Menses-Inducing Drugs: Their Role in Antique, Medieval and Renaissance Gynecology and Birth Control | author = Jöchlea, W. | journal = Contraception | volume = 10 | issue = 4 | year = 1974 | pages = 425–439 | doi = 10.1016/0010-7824(74)90042-0 | pmid = 4614935 }}</ref> The species has been suggested as a possible identity for the controversial [[Silphium (antiquity)|silphium]], a plant used as a spice and for various medical purposes in [[classical antiquity]] in the Mediterranean region.<ref>{{cite journal | title = The Silphium Motif Adorning Ancient Libyan Coinage: Marketing a Medicinal Plant |author1=Koerper, H. |author2=Kolls, A. L. | journal = Economic Botany | volume = 53 | issue = 2 | year = 1999 | pages = 133–143 | doi = 10.1007/BF02866492 | jstor = 4256173 |bibcode=1999EcBot..53..133K |s2cid=32144481 }}</ref> Among the many uses of silphium was promoting menstruation, and possibly [[contraceptive]] or [[abortifacient]] properties, which has been suggested to link it to ''[[Ferula]]''.
